subject: EU & APAC model validation handshake + next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Muller <sofia.muller@linguacorp.de>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:22:00+02:00
Subject: Intro + quick follow on today's discovery call: EU & JP locales

Hi Lauren / Neha / Ben,

Thanks again for the call earlier — very helpful. Quick recap from our side and a shortlist of asks so we can get a pilot started: 

1) Primary use cases: customer-support summarization (DE, FR), knowledge retrieval + response generation for in-product help (EN-UK, EN-US), and localized guided responses (JA).
2) Key quality concerns: legal/localized phrasing in German (compound nouns, formality), French idiomatic phrasing, and Japanese polite/formal registers (keigo). Small errors in honorifics or legal terms are blockers for compliance review.
3) Latency targets: ~350–450ms P95 for short responses (<= 128 tokens) in EU region; APAC can tolerate slightly higher latency for now but prefer <600ms P95.
4) Benchmark expectations: we’d like to see chrF >= 0.60 for DE/FR and human-rated adequacy >= 4/5 on a 150-sample prompt set before staging.

Can you share: model recommendations per locale (and fallback options), the prompt sets you suggest we run, a quick list of the benchmarks you’ll produce, and any obvious risks you foresee before we hand this to engineering? Also looping in procurement (procurement@linguacorp.de) — they may ask about reserved capacity pricing.

Attaching a short sample of the prompt buckets we used in the call.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Muller
Head of Localization, LinguaCorp

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Muller <sofia.muller@linguacorp.de>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@tokyoai.co.jp>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick follow on today's discovery call: EU & JP locales

Hi Sofia (and Kenji),

Appreciate the clear asks — below is a concise plan and model recommendations tailored to each locale. I’ll attach the detailed prompt sets and a short benchmark deck after internal alignment (see attachments list).

Summary & recommendations
- Germany / France (DE, FR): Primary recommendation = redwood-catalyst-13b-fp16. Rationale: strong quality/fluency tradeoff on European morphologically rich languages, predictable tokenization for German compounds, and good cost/latency when run fp16 on A100-class hardware. Fallback = redwood-catalyst-7b-int8 (faster, cheaper; expect ~3–5% lower chrF).
- English (EN-UK / EN-US): redwood-scout-6b for high throughput use cases (FAQ/autocomplete) and redwood-catalyst-13b for higher-quality doc summarization.
- Japanese (JA): redwood-kumo-8b-int8-jp (model variant with improved tokenization for kana/kanji sequences). Fallback = redwood-kumo-4b-quant (low-latency edge option).

Benchmarks we’ll produce (deliver within 4 business days):
- Locale-specific automatic metrics: chrF, BLEU, ROUGE-L on your supplied prompt buckets (per-locale split).
- Human fluency/adequacy readout on 150 samples (stratified by use case).
- Latency & cost profile (P50/P95 token latency + per-1M token cost) for each recommended variant and quantization setting.

Quality/regression concerns we’ll watch for
- German compound handling (split vs. join) — impacts entity extraction in legal text.
- French localized idioms causing decreased BLEU but may still be acceptable in human scoring — we’ll prioritize human evals.
- Japanese politeness/honorifics — small stylistic errors can be high impact; propose targeted prompt templates to control keigo levels.

Next steps / asks (action items)
1) We’ll run the initial automated benchmark on your sample prompt_buckets.csv and share a short results deck by 2027-04-26. (Redwood: Lauren & Neha)
2) Please share any additional target utterances that must be preserved exactly (legal terms, trademarks). (LinguaCorp: Sofia)
3) Procurement question: Ben, can you share a 3-month reserved capacity estimate for: 13B fp16 in EU region + 8B int8 in APAC? (Ben)
4) Schedule a 30-min technical readout with your eng team the week of 2027-05-03 — propose 2027-05-04 or 2027-05-06.

I’m attaching: eu_prompt_set_v2.csv (localized prompt templates), apac_prompt_jp_v1.csv (JP templates), and a short model recommendations PDF.

If that aligns, we’ll queue the runs and come back with the deck.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: eu_prompt_set_v2.csv (stub), apac_prompt_jp_v1.csv (stub), redwood_model_recs.pdf (stub)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-23T15:35:00+01:00
Subject: Re: EU & APAC model validation handshake + next steps

Thanks Lauren — quick technical follow up from the infra/evals side.

Planned eval cadence & tech notes
- Automated pass: run chrF/BLEU on the full prompt set (split by intent and length) and surface per-bucket deltas versus our baseline. Baseline will be redwood-catalyst-13b-fp16 for EU and redwood-kumo-8b-int8-jp for JP.
- Human eval: 150 samples (50 DE/50 FR/50 JA) split across three graders with a shared rubric: adequacy (1–5), fluency (1–5), and critical error flag (Y/N).
- Canary policy: we’ll stage a canary on dedicated capacity limited to 5% traffic for 48 hrs; rollback triggers are human score drop >0.5 or increase in critical error flags >2%.

Risks to highlight to LinguaCorp engineers
- Tokenization differences may inflate automatic metric variance for German compounds; recommend a secondary metric based on normalized entity matching (we can run).
- For Japanese: some quantized variants drop handling of polite verb endings — we’ll include specific prompt templates forcing keigo (e.g., explicit system prompts).

Deliverables and timing
- Automated benchmark XLSX (you’ll get one per locale) — 2027-04-26 EOD.
- Human eval summary and appendix with sample outputs — 2027-04-29.
- Short tech readout slide deck and recommended rollout checklist — ready by the readout meeting.

Ben — I’ll need the rough cost delta for fp16 vs int8 for the per-1M token view so procurement has numbers.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
